info.title: MaintenancePizza API
info.description:
Ticket system microservice for store maintenance. An authenticated user files a ticket describing the issues in a store; dispatchers then drive each issue through its lifecycle (diagnosis, technician assignment, attendance, parts, pay/driving, warranty) until completion.

Key design notes:
- All endpoints require a Sanctum bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`). There are no login/registration endpoints in this service — tokens are issued elsewhere.
- Most endpoints are store-scoped under `/api/stores/{store}`, where `{store}` is the store NUMBER (e.g. `03795-00001`), not a numeric id.
- The system is append-only apart from one exception: `PATCH .../issues/{ticketIssue}` re-points an issue at a different catalog issue. Everything else is corrected by marking leaf records `mistaken` and creating new ones; lifecycle changes are explicit POST actions.
- A ticket's status is DERIVED from its issues and is never set directly.
- Workflow records (diagnosis, attendance, parts, pay, warranty, assignment, technicians) attach to ONE OR MANY issues via `ticket_issue_ids`, enabling flexible grouping.
- Every entity (tickets, issues, workflow records, catalog items, stores) accepts any number of polymorphic Notes and Attachments via dedicated POST endpoints.
- Notes are stored with their author (`created_by`), optional `type`, and may carry their own file attachments.
- Ticket closing notes are typed with FinalNoteType (`final_notes` or `what_we_learned`) and are appended via the `/final-note` endpoint.
- Issues (and tickets by derivation) now support a `cancelled` status in addition to the existing statuses.

tags.name: Issue Workflow
tags.description: Per-issue lifecycle: status, deferral, cancellation, assignment, diagnosis, parts, pay, attendance, warranty

tags.name: Notes & Attachments
tags.description: Generic polymorphic notes and file attachments — the same POST shape is available on every entity (tickets, issues, all workflow records, stores, catalog items)

tags.name: Storage
tags.description: Parts inventory across one or more storage locations. Stock is an append-only ledger of movements: on-hand is SUM(quantity × direction) over every movement line, and a mistake is corrected by recording an equal-and-opposite reversal rather than by editing. Taking a part out of storage on a ticket writes a movement automatically.

tags.name: Daily Pay
tags.description:
End-of-day payment records, in three levels: an entry is one date, it holds one payment per payee, and each payment holds one line per store. A payee is a Technician row — a company is simply a technician named after the company — so a single payment can cover several stores at once.

Each payment gathers its own figures from records that already exist: the hours clocked against its issues, and the parts somebody other than us paid for. Those are FROZEN when the entry is saved, so a signed-off pay sheet does not change when a ticket is corrected later; POST .../recalculate re-pulls them on demand.

Editing replaces the payments wholesale while keeping a JSON snapshot of the prior state as revision history.

post.summary: Cancel an issue — records reason, no child spawned
post.description: Marks the issue `cancelled` (a terminal/finished status) and records the reason in `status_changes`. Unlike deferral it spawns no child. If every issue on the ticket ends up cancelled, the ticket derives to `cancelled`.

post.summary: Restore a retired storage location
Record a batch of stock moving (multipart, optional files)
post.description:
One movement is one batch: several parts, their amounts, where they are, and who paid. Most types imply their direction; `adjustment` moves either way, so each of its lines must state `direction` itself. A transfer is one movement with a -1 line at the source and a +1 line at the destination.

Taking stock below zero is refused with 422 and nothing is written. `reversal` cannot be posted directly — use the `/mistaken` action, which writes it for you.

storage_location_id.description: The movement's own location; each line still names its own

lines[0][quantity].description: Always a positive magnitude; `direction` says which way it moves

lines[0][direction].description: Required only for types that move both ways (adjustment); otherwise taken from the type

get.summary: Show one stock movement with its lines

post.summary: Correct a movement by recording its reversal
post.description:
Flags the movement and writes an equal-and-opposite `reversal`. The original row is never edited or removed — the ledger is append-only, and the flag itself has no effect on the arithmetic.

A reversal is allowed to take a balance negative: reversing a return pushes stock down, and that stock may since have been consumed. Refusing would leave the mistake uncorrectable. `php artisan stock:reconcile` lists any negative pairs.

200.description: The flagged original plus the reversal that was written

get.summary: What is on hand, per part per location
get.description: A cache of SUM(quantity × direction) over the movement ledger, kept in step inside the same transaction as every movement. `php artisan stock:reconcile` recomputes it from the ledger and reports any drift.

parameters.name: non_zero
parameters.description: Hide pairs that have netted back to nothing

post.summary: Add a note to a storage location
Attach files to a storage location
Add a note to a stock movement
Attach files to a stock movement
Re-gather the frozen hours and reimbursable parts
post.description:
Re-reads the attendance entries and reimbursable part usages behind every payment on this entry and rewrites the frozen figures from them.

Lines whose hours were supplied in the payload (`hours_overridden: true`) are left exactly as typed — only their `gathered` block is refreshed, so you can still see what the records say. Lines that were left to be gathered pick up the newer numbers.

Idempotent: running it twice changes nothing the second time.

200.description: The entry with its figures re-gathered

post.summary: Add an attendance entry spanning several tickets (multipart, optional files)
post.description: One visit, many tickets: a technician drives to a store once and works issues belonging to different tickets. Identical to the ticket-nested endpoint except that no parent ticket scopes the issues — they need only exist, and the technician must already be attached to at least one of them.

ticket_issue_ids[].description: Issue ids from any number of tickets

post.summary: Create a daily pay entry
post.description:
Creates a new end-of-day payment entry. Each `lines[]` element represents one technician working at one store. A technician who worked at multiple stores appears as multiple lines. Notes and file attachments can be included inline per line.

**Multipart form-data required** when uploading files. Field names use bracket notation: `lines[0][files][]`, `lines[0][notes][0][files][]`.

201.description: Created entry with all lines, notes, attachments, and linked ticket issues

get.description: Returns the full detail of a daily pay entry including all lines (with notes, attachments, and linked ticket issue IDs) and the complete revision history (snapshots of all previous states with who edited and when).

200.description: Full daily pay entry detail with revision history

post.summary: Edit a daily pay entry
post.description:
Replaces the full content of an existing daily pay entry. Before replacing, the current state is snapshot as a revision record (accessible in the `revisions` array). The same payload shape as create is accepted.

This is a **full replace** — all existing lines are dropped and recreated from the new payload. Any notes or attachments on old lines will not appear on the new lines unless re-submitted.

**Multipart form-data required** when uploading files.

200.description: Updated entry with new lines and a new revision record

FilterPaymentStatuses.name: payment_statuses[]
FilterPaymentStatuses.description: Whether a ticket’s work has been settled through a pay sheet (multi-select, OR logic). A payable is an attendance entry, or a part somebody other than us paid for; mistaken records never count. `unpaid` = at least one payable is still unclaimed, so use this to pull up everything still owed. `paid` = it has payables and every one of them is claimed. `not_payable` = it has no payables at all.

FilterTypes.description: Filter by ticket type (multi-select, OR logic)

FilterCreatorIds.name: creator_ids[]

IncludeAnalytics.name: include_analytics
IncludeAnalytics.description: Also compute and return an 'analytics' block (issue status breakdown, duration averages, weekly average) alongside the paginated list, scoped by the same active filters. Off by default.

NotFound.description: No such record, or it is out of scope for this store

DailyPayEntryInput.description: Sent as multipart/form-data with bracket-notation keys, e.g. payments[0][lines][0][store_id] and payments[0][lines][0][files][].

date.description: The workday this pay sheet covers (YYYY-MM-DD).

expected_updated_at.description: Edit only, and optional. Send back the updated_at you last read; if someone else has changed the entry since, the edit is refused with 409 instead of silently overwriting their figures.

payments.description: One element per payee. A payee may appear only once per sheet — put all of their stores on the one payment.

technician_id.description: Who is being paid. A company is a Technician row named after the company.

hourly_payment_rate.description: Default rate for this payment's lines; a line may state its own.

lump_sum.description: A flat amount INSTEAD OF hours × rate for the whole payment, not on top of it.

gas.description: Fuel that is not attributable to one store. Per-store fuel goes on the line.

money_owed.description: NOT the total. An optional extra amount we also owe them, added on top.

lines.description: One element per store this payment covers.

other_store.description: A location outside the replicated store list, named freely — the same escape hatch tickets have. Give a line either this or store_id.

total_working_hours.description: Leave out to have it gathered from the attendance entries on this line's issues. Supply it to override, and recalculate will then leave this line's hours alone.

travel_time.description: Paid at the hourly rate, like work time.

lump_sum.description: A flat amount for this store INSTEAD OF its hours × rate.

hourly_payment_rate.description: Overrides the payment's rate for this store.

ticket_issue_ids.description: The work this line pays for. The payee must already be assigned to each issue. These links are what the gather reads to find the hours and the reimbursable parts.

DailyPayGathered.description: Figures pulled from the attendance and part-usage records behind this payment's issues, frozen at save time and refreshed by POST .../recalculate.

work_hours.description: Net of breaks, parts runs and travel that fall inside the clock window

reimbursable_parts.description: Net cost of the parts somebody other than us paid for

DailyPayLineResource.description: One store's share of a payment.

technician_id.description: Always the same as the payment's payee; denormalised so store/payee filters stay one join deep.

hours_overridden.description: True when the hours above were supplied rather than gathered. recalculate leaves such a line's hours untouched.

line_total.description: What this store cost: labour (or its lump sum) + gas + money owed + the parts attributed to it.

DailyPayPaymentResource.description: One payment to one payee, covering however many stores.

money_owed.description: NOT the total — an optional extra we also owe them.

lines_total.description: Sum of the line totals. A per-store roll-up for display; total_amount is the payable figure.

total_amount.description: The payable figure: labour (or the payment's lump sum) + line gas and money owed + payment gas and money owed + the reimbursable parts, counted once at payment level.

aggregation_warnings.description: What the gather could not make sense of. Nothing here blocks the pay sheet; a person decides. Codes include overlapping_entries, entry_outside_date, part_usage_spans_stores, already_claimed_same_date, claimed_on_other_entry, and the attendance data warnings (incomplete_pair, inverted_pair, implausible_pair).

DailyPayEntrySummary.description: List view: payments and their money, without lines, notes, attachments or revisions.

DailyPayEntryRevisionResource.description: A snapshot of the entry's full state immediately before an edit.

snapshot.description: The entry as it stood before this edit, stored as JSON. Read schema_version before rendering it.

schema_version.description: 1 = the old two-level shape {date, lines: [...]}, written before payments existed. 2 = {date, payments: [{..., lines: [...]}]}. Snapshots are never rewritten, so both shapes exist in history.

Priority.description: Enum wrapper returned by the API for priority fields.

IssueStatus.description: Enum wrapper returned by the API for issue-level status fields.

TicketStatus.description: Enum wrapper for the derived ticket status. Never set directly.

FinalNoteType.description: Constrains the `type` field on ticket closing notes. 'final_notes' = general closing summary; 'what_we_learned' = lessons learned.

path.description: Relative path on the public storage disk

url.description: Full public URL — use this in / download links

files[].description: One or more files (max 10 MB each)

type.description: FinalNoteType value for ticket closing notes; null for generic notes on other entities.

type_label.description: Human-readable label for `type` when it matches a FinalNoteType; null otherwise.

attachments.description: Files attached to this note (e.g. a photo in a 'What we learned' note).

type.description: Optional free-form type string. On the ticket /final-note endpoint this must be a FinalNoteType value; on all other note endpoints it is unconstrained.

files[].description: Optional file(s) to attach to this note (max 10 MB each)
Optional file(s) to attach to this note (max 10 MB each)

from_status.description: Previous status value (null when the issue was first created).

reason.description: Required for deferrals and cancellations; null for plain status changes.

payment.description: Whether these hours have been settled through a pay sheet. Null when the claims were not loaded.

start_travel.description: Start of a travel leg (e.g. depot to store, or store to store)

durations.description: Derived from the clock pairs, never stored. `work` is net: break, parts-run and travel are merged and subtracted, but only the portion falling inside the clock window. The other three are reported at full recorded length. Bad data (a half-set pair, an end before its start, a pair over 24h) contributes zero or is clamped, and is reported in `warnings` rather than raising an error.

hours.description: The same figures rounded to 2dp for display

PaymentStatus.description: Whether a record that costs somebody money has been settled through a daily pay sheet. Being on a sheet IS being paid — there is no separate "money sent" step. Derived on read from the pay sheets themselves, so it can never disagree with them.

value.description: `unpaid` — owed, not yet on a pay sheet. `paid` — covered by one. `not_payable` — nothing for anyone to be paid back: a part we bought ourselves, or a record marked mistaken.

PaymentClaim.description: One payment that has counted this record.

daily_pay_line_id.description: The store line it was attributed to, or null when it could not be pinned to one store.

amount.description: Part usages only: what was reimbursed for this receipt.

minutes.description: Attendance entries only: the minutes this payment counted.

PaymentState.description: A record’s payment position: its status, and which payments settled it.

direction.description: -1 out of the location, +1 into it

signed_quantity.description: quantity × direction — what this line contributes to the balance

part_usage_id.description: Set when this movement was generated by a part usage rather than recorded by hand

mistaken.description: Display only — flagged movements still count toward the balance, because the reversal is what corrects it

quantity.description: May be negative when a reversal was applied after the stock had been consumed

cost.description: GROSS total outlay = quantity × unit_cost, as a decimal string (2 places), e.g. "49.99". This is the figure the part_cost_single_gt / part_cost_total_gt ticket filters sum. Use net_cost for the after-returns figure.

net_quantity.description: quantity − returned_quantity: how many were actually consumed

net_cost.description: What the payer is really out of pocket once returns are taken off. This, not `cost`, is what a daily pay reimburses.

reimbursable.description: True when someone other than us paid and is owed the money back

stock_movement_ids.description: The movements this usage generated in the stock ledger, if any

payment.description: Whether whoever paid for this has had it back through a pay sheet. A part we bought ourselves reads as not_payable — there is nobody to reimburse.

mistaken.description: Flagging a usage as a mistake puts any stock it moved back, by writing reversal movements. The originals are left exactly as recorded.
True when this record was entered in error.
True when this delay record was entered in error.
True when this record was entered in error.

TicketIssue.description: A single issue line on a ticket, with its full workflow history when returned from the /issues endpoints.

issue_id.description: Catalog issue id; null when other_title was used instead.

display_title.description: The catalog issue title or other_title — always non-null.

payment.description: Whether everything this issue costs anybody is on a pay sheet yet. Anything still owed dominates, so the issue reads as unpaid until the last of its payables is settled. Null when the records it reads were not loaded.

daily_pay_line_ids.description: The pay lines that cover this issue.

parent_id.description: Set when this is a deferred child. Points to the parent TicketIssue.

Ticket.description: A maintenance ticket. Status is derived from its issues and never stored.

store_id.description: Null for tickets filed under 'Others' (no known store).

other_store.description: Free-text store description for 'Others' tickets. Null for normal store-scoped tickets.

notes.description: All notes on the ticket. Closing notes have a non-null `type` (FinalNoteType). Generic notes have type=null.

analytics.description: Present only when include_analytics=true was passed

total.description: Issues matching the active filters (i.e. 'new' issues when scoped via a date filter)

status_breakdown.description: All 7 IssueStatus values always present, zero-filled when absent. status_breakdown[status=complete].count is 'how many completed'.

durations.description: Averages in seconds/hours; null with sample_size 0 when no issue matches

avg_tickets_per_week.description: Always all-time (ignores created_from/to and changed_from/to; still respects every other active filter). Custom week runs Tuesday 00:00:00 through Monday 23:59:59.

weeks_spanned.description: Weeks between the earliest and latest matching ticket, inclusive; weeks with zero tickets still count

TicketType.description: Ticket type: normal issue or preventive maintenance.

type.description: Ticket type. Defaults to 'normal' when omitted.

issues.description: One or more issue lines. Each line uses either a catalog issue_id OR a free-text other_title.

issue_id.description: Catalog issue id. Provide this OR other_title, not both.

other_title.description: Free-text issue title. Required when issue_id is absent.

notes.description: Optional notes to attach to this issue at creation time (text only; use POST …/notes to add files to notes afterward).

issues.*.files[].description: Files to attach directly to this issue (multipart only — field name issues[N][files][]).

notes.description: Optional notes to attach to the ticket itself at creation time.

files[].description: Files to attach directly to the ticket (requires multipart/form-data).

other_store.description: Free-text description of the location or store not present in the system.

type.description: Ticket type. Defaults to 'normal' when omitted.

issues.description: One or more issue lines. Each line uses either a catalog issue_id OR a free-text other_title.

issue_id.description: Catalog issue id. Provide this OR other_title, not both.

other_title.description: Free-text issue title. Required when issue_id is absent.

notes.description: Optional notes to attach to the ticket itself at creation time.
